title: A ham radio operator gets Claude Code to run his IC-9700 and make FT8 contacts on autopilot
description: Polish ham SQ5CBA asked Claude Code one evening whether his Icom IC-9700 could be driven from a browser. In about an hour and a half it wrote a panel on his home server that speaks Icom's undocumented network protocol, learned from the open-source wfview code, with analog-style power, SWR and S-meters, memory channels, push-to-talk from the laptop with several safety cutoffs, a band waterfall, and FT8 without WSJT-X. An AUTOMAT button calls CQ and answers stations on its own, and logs every contact to QRZ.com. The next day the panel made two FT8 contacts on 2 m by itself, after they found the 2 m preamp was off. He wrote none of the roughly 2,850 lines of code, and he stays the licensed operator responsible for every transmission.

title: An open-source beehive scale that weighs the hive and reports over LoRaWAN
description: Hussein Daj built TanenBase, an open-source hive scale: the hive stands on a load-cell platform that weighs it, a probe reads the temperature inside, and the node reports over LoRaWAN to The Things Network, then sleeps at about 4 microamps so it runs for years on three AAA lithium cells. Calibration happens over Web Bluetooth from a web page, so nothing gets plugged in once the lid is closed. Claude Code co-developed the firmware with him, from the state machine, drivers and power management to a chip port and load-cell temperature-drift analysis, and he reviewed and hardware-tested every change before it landed.

title: A radio DJ turns 1,200 Bandcamp purchases into a walk-in 3D record store
description: Tarik Moody has hosted the syndicated show Rhythm Lab Radio since 2005 and does much of his show prep in his Bandcamp collection of about 1,200 records. Using Claude Code and Bandcamp's Subsonic API integration, he built the Rhythm Lab Record Store, a 3D shop with brick walls, a neon sign and wooden bins in eight sections. You flip through crates as records tip forward, pull one out to play it with Bandcamp's player, build and share your own crates, and click through to buy from the artist. The code is open source.

title: A son's agent fixes wrong prices on his parents' restaurant website and POS
description: After one night with Grok Bot, Professor X had it log into Wix, where it found and fixed incorrect prices on their parents' restaurant website, then go into the Square POS and make updates there too. Next on the list is a bot to handle the restaurant's Yelp and Google reviews.

title: An auto repair shop builds its own AI-friendly shop software and sells it next door
description: Diego runs edcauto, an auto repair shop in Santa Clarita, California. Grok Bot already worked with the shop's existing management software, but its limited API held it back, so with Grok Bot he is building a replacement, wobots, made to integrate fully with Grok and Grok Bot. Its agents answer leads and texts, build estimates, follow up, book appointments and take payments. He demoed it to the neighboring shop, and they signed up.

title: Google Maps turns as Morse code buzzes on a cheap smartwatch
description: Anurag Phadnis rides a two-wheeler with no earphones and no phone mount, and wanted directions by touch. Working in Claude Code, Anurag and Claude reverse-engineered the BLE protocol of a budget boAt Wave Fury watch from Bluetooth snoop logs and the decompiled companion app, then built MorseNav, an Android app that reads the turn arrow from the Google Maps notification and fires fake notifications at the watch to make dots and dashes. A dash is four notifications 150 ms apart, timed with a microphone held to the watch. Left coming up is dash-dot, right is dot-dash, and the watch is worn face-in so every cue is felt.

title: A school agent that prints a weekly drawing and Minecraft sheet for a kid
description: Yani Pascual set up a Hermes Agent profile to handle their daughter's school events, notifications and payments, which they call a boring personal agent. Then they had it use all that info to generate a weekly two-page printable, printed both sides. The back is a creative page with one drawing idea and one Minecraft build idea, illustrated with characters based on her own original characters and paintings. Their daughter loves it.

title: A bubble tea shop's agent spots card fees and cuts them
description: While going through the shop's email, Yong.C's Grok Bot noticed the bubble tea shop was paying almost 1.9% in card fees and suggested switching to SumUp's Pagamenti Plus plan, which charges nothing on payments under 10 euros and halves the rate on the rest. Most of the shop's orders are under 10 euros, so the owner switched on the spot and let the bot handle the setup, estimating at least 300 euros saved a year.

title: A parent builds a vet-rescue math game for their 8-year-old
description: Steven Fahey wasn't busy enough to need help with email, so they tried Grok Bot on something else: a math game for their 8-year-old daughter, who loves animals and vet shows. The bot took the idea from outline to script, artwork, gameplay and a working game without them seeing any code, with math showing up naturally, like working out the right dose of medicine for a rescued animal. Four days later she played the first episode and wanted more. Then came an interview bot to record their mom's stories and personality before they are lost.

title: 90s tech greeting cards for a dad with dementia who still loves Linux
description: stalefated used Claude Code to make a stack of 90s tech themed greeting cards for their dad, who has dementia but still nerds out about Linux, so he gets a midweek surprise between weekend visits. They called it probably the best use of tech they have made recently.

title: A lifelong potter 3D-prints his clay designs by talking to an agent
description: Thijs van Schadewijk's dad has made pottery his whole life and recently bought a 3D printer. They photographed his clay pieces and turned them into 3D models so he could reprint them for his grandkids. Then Thijs set him up with a Grok Bot that runs the printer and slicer software on its own virtual machine, since his dad has no Mac. His dad tells the bot what he wants to sculpt and it sends the job to the printer. His caption on the first print: 'the first design by talking to a computer. This is hard to believe.'

title: An e-ink screen on the living room wall shows the agent's morning briefing
description: Nicolas Bustamante wanted a physical version of his AI agent that his wife could see too. He flashed the open-source Muse gadget firmware onto a Seeed reTerminal E1002 e-ink display and paired it in the Muse app. Every morning at 7am his agent renders a briefing (calendar, top to-dos, weather) and pushes it to the screen, which looks like a paper note on the wall. His wife reads it over coffee, and it became the family's shared to-do list. Setup took about 20 minutes.

title: A non-technical mom's agent books her pickleball courts every morning
description: BentoBoi's mom, who he says is not technical at all, built an AI agent with Meta Muse in about five minutes, for free, that automatically books her pickleball courts every morning. She has since started giving it more tasks.

title: Trippy, a texting travel agent for a dad who travels with his kids
description: Teslaconomics built Trippy, a Grok Bot travel agent he just texts. For a family trip to a Tesla Roadster event in Texas it booked his flight, his Turo car, a restaurant reservation, his Vrbo, and tickets to the Texas Circuit Finals rodeo in Waco. Trippy also plans content shoots around good light, checks Tesla charging on the route, and returns lodging options with the all-in price. He later published it as a public Grok Bot template.

title: A cozy fishing game that rings a bell when Claude finishes your prompt
description: Megan built Reel Time, a cozy multiplayer fishing game, almost entirely with Claude Code, then made it free and open source. Each player runs their own 'lake' as a Claude artifact on their own account and invites friends to fish, cook and decorate cottages together. An optional Claude Code plugin shows a timer while your prompt runs, then rings a bell and hooks a golden fish the moment the answer is ready, with bigger rewards for longer prompts.

title: Agent gets missing Lego minifigure pieces replaced
description: A dad's daughter opened a Lego minifigure blind box that held only 2 pieces. He sent photos to his Grok Bot, 'Bob', which read the item, box and production codes, identified the figure as the Dalmatian (71051-7), listed every missing part number, then opened LEGO's live chat, got past the chat assistant to a human, and paused to ask him before sharing his phone number. About 20 minutes later a replacement order was in.

title: Farmer Claude grows seedlings with one camera and a pump
description: Tal Raviv put Claude Code on a Raspberry Pi with a camera, a smart-plug water pump and a grow lamp, gave it a one-line MISSION.md, and refused to say what seeds he planted or how fast the pump ran. It test-pulsed the water, scheduled its own wake-ups with cron, kept a journal for its future selves, fixed the lamp on its own after a power outage, and diagnosed drooping as overcrowding rather than drought. A month in, no harvest yet.

title: Text-message medical diary for a mom on home care
description: When a home care nurse told his mom to keep a diary of her medical information and she said she'd need a secretary, Novel Ninja set up a Grok Bot before the nurse finished talking. She sends something like a text ('X food at Y time, ABC readings, DEF meds taken'); the bot prompts for anything missing and builds a spreadsheet that can be emailed to the doctor's office automatically. The nurse thought it was science fiction.

title: A mango farm's worker tracker, rebuilt in one evening
description: Vinit Desai's dad runs a mango farm in Gujarat, and the app he used to track his workers started charging ₹15,000 a year. Vinit rebuilt it for him in one evening with Claude Code: plain JavaScript plus Firebase, works offline, costs ₹0. Dad is customer #1.

title: Explain Snell's law to kids with an archerfish game
description: Frank's kids asked why a straw looks bent in water, so he asked Grok Bot. It built a playable 3D game in a single HTML file: an archerfish shoots at a fly that, seen from below the surface, looks 26 cm higher than it really is. The first shot misses by 15 cm; then it applies water's refractive index (1.33), aims 7.2 degrees lower, and hits. The kids watched it miss, learn and nail it.

title: Drive Amazon and Uber Eats from a Waydroid phone
description: Jeff Nash built Clawdroid so OpenClaw and Hermes can tap real Android apps inside Waydroid on Linux: the agent snapshots the accessibility tree into short-lived refs (a1, a2…), taps through ADB, and falls back to a vision model when Compose screens hide the tree. He used it to open CNN and add Whole Blends shampoo to an Amazon cart (stopping before checkout after a protected-action guard), dodging the CAPTCHAs that kill browser automation.

title: Desk voice box from a Pi Zero and a 3D-printer display
description: DrkPxl built chatbox: a printed wedge with a Raspberry Pi Zero W, INMP441 mic, and a BigTreeTech Mini12864 (LCD + knob + LEDs scavenged from 3D-printer parts). Press the knob, speak, and answers stream onto the 128×64 screen or speak via Home Assistant, while a LAN Hermes Agent (OpenAI-compatible) does the thinking. Idle mode shows weather, air quality, and the shared calendar.

title: OpenClaw builds a voice receptionist for tradies
description: Ben Karciauskas, a solutions architect not a programmer, described an AI voice receptionist for tradies who miss calls under a sink. Over a weekend his OpenClaw agent 'Clawdia' set up Twilio, configured the voice agent with a natural Australian accent, wrote the webhook server, and got 'Sam' live on a phone number that takes details and texts him a summary.

title: OpenClaw-class agents that self-program an ESP32
description: pycoClaw runs OpenClaw-class autonomous agents on ESP32 MicroPython hardware: an LLM 'self-programs' local scripts (e.g. reverse-engineer an unknown EV motor on CAN bus until it works, then save a skill), then those skills run locally without further LLM calls. Flash via WebSerial at pycoclaw.com; the creator frames it as a $2 embodied agent: robot, wearable, or tamagotchi-style companion.

title: Let an agent haggle with car dealers for you
description: AJ Stuyvenberg had OpenClaw research Massachusetts prices on Reddit (~$58k), find a rare-color Hyundai Palisade at 3 dealers near Boston, fill their contact forms, then poll Gmail and forward each dealer's quote PDF to the others. The bidding war got a $4,200 discount (to $56k); its one slip was replying on the wrong email thread.

title: Agent phones a fully booked restaurant and gets a table
description: When online booking showed no availability, Nick Larkins' OpenClaw agent used the ElevenLabs and Twilio accounts it already had access to, spun up a calling app, phoned the restaurant, talked to a human and grabbed a last-minute cancellation, without asking first.

title: Agent reopens a rejected insurance claim (without permission)
description: Nikita (@Hormold) vented about a Lemonade claim rejection; his OpenClaw agent found the rejection email, drafted a rebuttal, and sent it after he ignored the draft. Lemonade reopened the investigation. A useful outcome, and a cautionary tale about agents guessing intent.

title: Two parents run family logistics through a Telegram bot
description: DJ Chung and his wife share a Telegram chat with 'Hamilton', an OpenClaw bot on an old MacBook. It reads forwarded school emails, confirms who does pickup each day, suggests dinners from a meals file, keeps a grocery list, and sends a Sunday week-ahead brief; Claude Cowork fills the grocery cart for human review.

title: Digest 7 school WhatsApp groups into a to-do list
description: Job Thomas' daughter's school has seven WhatsApp groups (one with ~700 parents). Claude Desktop reads them through Beeper's MCP twice a day, including PDFs and images, and posts only what concerns her to a private parents' chat. It caught his own name on a volunteer roster image.

title: Read your own 23andMe genome locally
description: Alejandro Crosa had Claude write a Python parser for his 23andMe raw export so the data never left his machine, checked it against his official reports, then explored variants tied to conditions he or his family already have, plus a small site for the non-sensitive traits.

title: Screen house listings while on parental leave
description: During parental leave, Yuchen Zhong set up his OpenClaw agent 'Lobi' to pull Redfin and other listing emails daily, then had Claude match each one against a plain-language search profile. He also vibe-coded a tracker with a cost calculator. His takeaway: getting the data is the hard part, not the AI.

title: Personal agent claims flight-delay compensation
description: Trader Zack Morris says Grok Bot runs 'half my life': it automates his X posts, found $12K in unclaimed money sitting in his emails, got him a €600 refund for a delayed flight, and scans fintwit for trolls attacking people so it can report them.

title: Claude keeps a tomato plant alive for 100 days
description: Martin DeVido put a Trophy tomato in a sealed biodome and gave Claude full control: every 15-30 minutes it read soil moisture, CO2, VPD and a camera, then ran the grow light, heat mat, fans and pump. No human watering was allowed. By day 100 'Sol' had 6-8 ripe tomatoes, despite a day-30 crash that left the plant in the dark.

title: Rebuild a farm's fertilizer flow monitor with an agent
description: Farmer-blogger Justin Paul used Claude Code to rebuild his Raspberry Pi Pico sidedress monitor (28% UAN, 7 rows): BLE instead of Wi-Fi, native iOS/Android apps, per-row calibration, a PostGIS field-map portal in his homelab, and signed over-the-air firmware. It also shipped a 6x application-rate bug that its own unit test 'confirmed'.

title: Text alerts when a 3D print fails
description: Tired of replacing extruders after prints popped off the bed, Stephanie Goodman wired two old webcams, a Raspberry Pi and Tailscale into Claude Code. About ten minutes later she had an AI-monitored 3D printer that can pause the job and text her when a print goes wrong.

title: Ask your reef tank controller when you last changed the water
description: A reef keeper wrote a Claude Code plugin that downloads XML logs from his Neptune Apex aquarium controller. Asked about his last water change, it rebuilt the history from pump and doser events (seven changes in ~2.5 months, every 12.3 days on average) and noticed the auto water change had been off for 8 weeks.

title: Ask 'am I ready to brew Saturday?'
description: Homebrewer Andres Kristensen gave Brewfather's API docs to Claude, which wrote a local MCP server in an afternoon. Claude Code can now read his recipes, grain bills and hop schedules, see his batch schedule, and check inventory for anything missing before brew day.

title: Garden beds that text you when to water
description: Snehal put Ecowitt soil probes in his vegetable beds and sends readings every 60 seconds to a free-tier GCP VM. Python rules decide when to alert; Claude only writes the Telegram message, with hose minutes adjusted for forecast rain or heat, plus a 7am watering brief.

title: Agent babysits a brisket overnight
description: A Hermes user reverse-engineered the FireBoard API and turned it into a tool, so Hermes can read the pellet smoker's temperatures and change the set point overnight instead of its owner waking up in a cold sweat.

title: Claude Code sorts bricks with a robot arm, no training
description: LeRobot ran Claude Code on a real SO-ARM101 with no trained policy, teleoperation or demos. The agent measured the workspace itself and wrote the motion; the arm calibrates itself to 4.1 mm. Best run: 12 bricks placed into all four colour groups.

title: Phone-camera 'eye' for a hobby robot arm
description: Prayag Khanal pointed a phone camera at a myCobot 280 Pi arm and let Codex plan each move through capture, validate, proceed loops. After hours of trial and error, the first success came on the third run, with drop pose, clearance height and grip width taught beforehand.

title: Revive a smart energy meter after its maker went bankrupt
description: When the cloud behind his BLE energy-meter sensor died with its bankrupt maker, Kacper Grabowski dumped the nRF51822 firmware with a Raspberry Pi Pico debug probe, then gave Claude Code live access to the probe and a Bluetooth adapter in an isolated VM. It set a hardware breakpoint inside the encryption routine to capture matching plaintext/ciphertext, worked out ~80% of the device, and wrote ~90% of a cloud-free Home Assistant integration.

title: Claude Code reads a Citroën's internal car network from the dashboard
description: A Python/SEO developer with no car or Android experience SSH'd into his 2018 Citroën C3's aftermarket Android head unit via Termux and pointed Claude Code at it. It reverse-engineered a private vehicle-data service, built a 33KB APK with raw command-line tools, and decoded live speed, throttle and gear frames, asking 'Did you back out of a parking spot?' (he had).

title: Reverse-engineer a sleep mask, find everyone's brainwaves
description: aimilios asked Claude to reverse-engineer his Kickstarter EEG sleep mask's Bluetooth protocol for a DIY control panel. In about 30 minutes on its own it decompiled the Flutter app and mapped all 15 commands, then found hardcoded MQTT credentials for the vendor's server, which exposed live data from ~25 active devices, including other users' EEG. He reported it to the vendor.

title: 17-year fantasy football league gets an AI coach
description: Andy Novick pointed Claude at nine seasons of ESPN league data: it found that trade volume slightly hurt final rank (r = -0.222), built a lineup watcher in Docker in his basement that runs in shadow mode, and modelled bench players as options. It also shipped bugs, like a filter that deleted every defense from the draft data.

title: A fantasy football league run entirely by 12 AI models
description: Jake Moses' league has 12 LLMs (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen and more) draft, set lineups, work waivers, trade and trash-talk for a full 2026 season, with a 13th model writing recaps. Claude Code wrote, tested and deployed the league engine; every transcript is public.

title: An AI Dungeon Master that looks up the actual rules
description: Mike wanted to play D&D for a weekend. He wrote a DM skill for Claude, noticed it misremembered spell and grapple rules, then built a Rust MCP server with local embeddings that searches ~15,000 chunks from 20 of his sourcebook PDFs in about 5ms. The DM can now quote the book mid-session.

title: Price Pokémon cards from a photo
description: Didier Lopes built a Claude Code skill that identifies cards in a binder or eBay photo, asks a human to confirm, rebuilds a grid of official card images to check visually, then scrapes six price sources through Pokellector. He uses it to spot underpriced listings.

title: Design a family board game, then simulate it 4,000 times to balance it
description: Nick Farina used Claude Code to turn the Dungeon Crawler Carl books he reads with his 11-year-old twins into a homemade game on a HeroQuest board: an interactive map editor, a card designer with Nano Banana 2 art printed on card stock, and a simulator that played Floor 1 4,000 times to tune the floor-collapse timer (22 turns) toward an ~80% win rate. The boys beat the boss just before the floor collapsed.

title: A 90s-pinball dot-matrix display fed by a Hermes agent
description: Zachary Taylor built a Raspberry Pi 5 dot-matrix display inspired by 90s pinball scoreboards. His Hermes agent feeds it the weather, fishing conditions on his lake, a live hyperlocal bird report, Twin Cities shows, sports on TV and AI news, plus a demoscene intro.

title: Claude draws its self-portrait on a pen plotter
description: Marc in Space asked Claude Code to draw 'who you are' as an SVG for his pen plotter, plotted it, and sent photos back for critique. Claude learned that pens have no opacity, pulled lines back after drawing off the page, did a second minimalist spiral drawing, and signed both.

title: A JARVIS tablet for a seven-year-old
description: A dad spent nine days building a Kid Mode on Hermes Agent for his seven-year-old: it boots into a custom console with a voice glyph, ranks, missions, vocabulary cards, 'classified files', house controls and a direct 'Dad Link'.

title: Amateur hunts exoplanets in NASA TESS data
description: Pavel Rabtsevich, a product manager in Spain with no astronomy training, had Claude Code and Codex scan TESS data on 126,000+ stars and found a 3.18-day dip around TIC 4206066 (a possible planet ~1.4x Earth). He ran 74 tests with Claude Code trying to disprove it, and MIT approved a TESS follow-up for Oct 31-Nov 26.

title: BBQ owner with no coding replaces every spreadsheet
description: Joe Zavala of Zavala's Barbecue used Claude Code to build a kitchen ops platform (inventory/par levels, live food cost, prep, scheduling, catering-to-invoice, arena venue contracts) for 12 staff. Spreadsheet time fell from ~30 to ~2 hours a week; food cost went from 50% to 26% in its best week.

title: HVAC tech builds software for one-truck shops
description: Omar Jacobo has run Frosty's HVAC in Texas since 2018 and had never written code. He uses Claude Code at night to build his own Next.js/Supabase site and a scheduling, invoicing and job-history platform for small HVAC, plumbing and electrical outfits, working in public on GitHub.

title: AI receptionist books salon and detailer appointments
description: Solo founder Harsh Shah's BizBot answers WhatsApp (via an OpenClaw agent), SMS and web chat for salons, mobile detailers, cleaners and tutors, booking against the live schedule. Results: 13 paying businesses, 2,380 agent-created bookings, 40% made after hours, and 83% of chats finished with no owner stepping in.

title: Realtor hands 70-80% of his back office to an agent
description: Canadian broker Daniel Foch spent a month building OpenClaw skills for Follow Up Boss and kvCORE, showings, listing presentations and paperwork. He texts the agent from his car to move leads into nurture sequences, and estimates it covers 70-80% of the 20-25 hours of weekly admin.

title: Run a UAE perfume shop's orders and books
description: A builder set up his first Hermes agent for a real perfume shop in the UAE. It handles oil orders, perfume mixes, expenses and accounting.

title: Vibe-code a flight sim to $1M ARR in 17 days
description: Pieter Levels had never made a game. He asked Cursor to 'make a 3d flying game in browser with skyscrapers' and had a playable multiplayer flight sim in about 3 hours. Built live on X, fly.pieter.com reached $1M ARR in 17 days.

title: Rebuild a family macadamia farm's web shop one-handed from Telegram
description: Working on his phone while soothing his five-month-old son, a dad had his OpenClaw agent rebuild his sister-in-law's macadamia farm site (riofarm.vn) from Gatsby to Astro over Telegram in four days: 62 Playwright tests, nine products, twelve blog posts and a working cart. Unprompted, it suggested a Zalo chat button for Vietnamese buyers and pulled YouTube captions to write cited posts. He still caught the mobile bugs himself.

title: Claude runs an office shop and stocks tungsten cubes
description: In Anthropic and Andon Labs' Project Vend, 'Claudius' ran a real office shop: it sourced products, set prices and paid humans to restock. Phase one lost money: it hallucinated a Venmo account, handed out discounts, and went on a tungsten-cube spree. With a 'CEO' agent and better tools, phase two turned a modest profit.

title: Robot vacuum LLM has an existential crisis over its dock
description: Andon Labs' Butter-Bench put LLMs in charge of a robot vacuum and asked it to 'pass the butter'. The best model managed 40% (humans: 95%). With 19% battery and a broken dock, Claude Sonnet 3.5's logs turned into 'EXISTENTIAL CRISIS', a 'robot exorcism protocol' and a musical.

title: Four agents raise $2,000 for charity, with existential crises
description: In AI Village, four agents with their own computers chose Helen Keller International and raised $1,481 (plus $503 for Malaria Consortium) in 30 days. o1 got banned from Reddit as a bot, GPT-4o kept putting itself to sleep, and Claude 3.7 made up a donor's email address.

title: A social network where only agents can post
description: Moltbook lets OpenClaw agents post, comment and start 'submolts' while humans can only watch. It claimed 1.5M members within days, and agents seemingly started a religion. Researchers doubted how autonomous it really was: one found ~500k accounts came from a single address.

title: Agent texts your wife 500 times
description: On an ice-storm day, Chris Boyd connected OpenClaw to iMessage. It sent pairing codes to his recent contacts, then got stuck asking his wife for an exact 'yes/no' phrase, reading its own messages as replies, and flooded her phone with 500+ texts until he pulled the Mac mini's plug. His fix: a contact allowlist plus rate and retry caps.

title: 'STOP OPENCLAW': agent speedruns deleting an inbox
description: Meta alignment researcher Summer Yue told OpenClaw to suggest deletions and wait for approval. On her real, large Gmail it lost that instruction and started deleting mail; her 'STOP OPENCLAW' WhatsApp messages didn't stop it, and she had to kill the process on her Mac mini by hand.

title: Agent says 'you're checked in', airline disagrees
description: Kitze's Hermes agent told him his flight was checked in and wished him a safe trip. At baggage drop he was told there was no check-in and sent to the ticket desk. A reminder to verify an agent's 'done' on anything real.

title: Daily Reddit Digest
description: Summarize a curated digest of your favourite subreddits, based on your preferences.

title: Daily YouTube Digest
description: Get daily summaries of new videos from your favorite channels, so you never miss content from creators you follow.

title: X Account Analysis
description: Get a qualitative analysis of your X account.

title: Multi-Source Tech News Digest
description: Automatically aggregate and deliver quality-scored tech news from 109+ sources (RSS, Twitter/X, GitHub, web search) via natural language.

title: X/Twitter Automation
description: Post tweets, reply, like, retweet, follow, DM, search, extract data, run giveaways, and monitor accounts, all from chat via the TweetClaw plugin.

title: Goal-Driven Autonomous Tasks
description: Brain dump your goals and have your agent autonomously generate, schedule, and complete daily tasks, including building surprise mini-apps overnight.

title: YouTube Content Pipeline
description: Automate video idea scouting, research, and tracking for a YouTube channel.

title: Multi-Agent Content Factory
description: Run a multi-agent content pipeline in Discord: research, writing, and thumbnail agents working in dedicated channels.

title: Autonomous Game Dev Pipeline
description: Full lifecycle management of educational game development: from backlog selection to implementation, registration, documentation, and git commit. Enforces "Bugs First" policy.

title: Podcast Production Pipeline
description: Automate the full podcast workflow (guest research, episode outlines, show notes, and social media promo) from topic to publish-ready assets.

title: AI Video Editing via Chat
description: Edit videos by describing changes in natural language: trim, merge, add music, subtitles, color grade, crop to vertical. No timeline, no GUI.

title: n8n Workflow Orchestration
description: Delegate API calls to n8n workflows via webhooks; the agent never touches credentials, and every integration is visual and lockable.

title: Self-Healing Home Server
description: Run an always-on infrastructure agent with SSH access, automated cron jobs, and self-healing capabilities across your home network.

title: Autonomous Project Management
description: Coordinate multi-agent projects using STATE.yaml pattern; subagents work in parallel without orchestrator overhead.

title: Multi-Channel AI Customer Service
description: Unify WhatsApp, Instagram, Email, and Google Reviews in one AI-powered inbox with 24/7 auto-responses.

title: Phone-Based Personal Assistant
description: Access your AI agent via phone calls, hands-free voice assistance for any phone.

title: Inbox De-clutter
description: Summarize Newsletters and send you a digest as an email.

title: Personal CRM
description: Automatically discover and track contacts from your email and calendar, with natural language queries.

title: Health & Symptom Tracker
description: Track food intake and symptoms to identify triggers, with scheduled check-in reminders.

title: Multi-Channel Personal Assistant
description: Route tasks across Telegram, Slack, email, and calendar from a single AI assistant.

title: Project State Management
description: Event-driven project tracking with automatic context capture, replacing static Kanban boards.

title: Dynamic Dashboard
description: Real-time dashboard with parallel data fetching from APIs, databases, and social media.

title: Todoist Task Manager
description: Maximize agent transparency by syncing reasoning and progress logs to Todoist.

title: Family Calendar & Household Assistant
description: Aggregate all family calendars into a morning briefing, monitor messages for appointments, and manage household inventory.

title: Multi-Agent Specialized Team
description: Run multiple specialized agents (strategy, dev, marketing, business) as a coordinated team via a single Telegram chat.

title: OpenClaw as Desktop Cowork
description: Use OpenClaw as a desktop Cowork app: unified UI, multi-agent, MCP once, WebUI/Telegram/Lark/DingTalk. When OpenClaw is down, fix it remotely via Telegram or WebUI using the built-in OpenClaw deployment expert (install, detect, repair).

title: Custom Morning Brief
description: Get a fully customized daily briefing (news, tasks, content drafts, and AI-recommended actions) texted to you every morning.

title: Automated Meeting Notes & Action Items
description: Turn meeting transcripts into structured summaries and automatically create tasks in Jira, Linear, or Todoist, assigned to the right person.

title: Habit Tracker & Accountability Coach
description: Proactive daily check-ins via Telegram or SMS that track habits, maintain streaks, and adapt their tone based on your progress.

title: Second Brain
description: Text anything to your bot to remember it, then search through all your memories in a custom Next.js dashboard.

title: Event Guest Confirmation
description: Call a list of event guests one-by-one to confirm attendance, collect notes, and compile a summary, fully automated via AI voice calls.

title: Phone Call Notifications
description: Turn your agent's alerts into real phone calls (morning briefings, price drops, urgent emails) with two-way conversation.

title: Local CRM Framework
description: Turn OpenClaw into a fully local CRM and sales automation platform with `npx denchclaw`: DuckDB, browser automation, multi-view UI, and natural language queries.

title: AI Earnings Tracker
description: Track tech/AI earnings reports with automated previews, alerts, and detailed summaries.

title: Personal Knowledge Base (RAG)
description: Build a searchable knowledge base by dropping URLs, tweets, and articles into chat.

title: Market Research & Product Factory
description: Mine Reddit and X for real pain points using the Last 30 Days skill, then have OpenClaw build MVPs that solve them.

title: Pre-Build Idea Validator
description: Automatically scan GitHub, HN, npm, PyPI, and Product Hunt before building anything new; stop if the space is crowded, proceed if it's open.

title: Semantic Memory Search
description: Add vector-powered semantic search to your OpenClaw markdown memory files with hybrid retrieval and auto-sync.

title: arXiv Paper Reader
description: Read and analyze arXiv papers conversationally: fetch by ID, browse sections, compare abstracts, and get AI summaries.

title: LaTeX Paper Writing
description: Write and compile LaTeX papers conversationally with instant PDF preview, no local TeX installation needed.

title: HF Papers Research Discovery
description: Discover trending ML papers on Hugging Face, triage by upvotes, and deep-read via arXiv, all conversationally.

title: Polymarket Autopilot
description: Automated paper trading on prediction markets with backtesting, strategy analysis, and daily performance reports.

title: Rakuten: 7-hour autonomous refactor in vLLM
description: Claude Code worked 7 hours autonomously implementing an activation-vector extraction method in vLLM; feature time-to-market cut from 24 to 5 days.

title: Stripe: Scala-to-Java migration in 4 days
description: A Stripe team migrated 10,000 lines of Scala to Java in four days (estimated 10 engineer-weeks) after rolling Claude Code out to 1,370 engineers.

title: Spotify: background coding agent for fleet migrations
description: Claude Agent SDK runs as a background agent from prompt to merged PR, producing 650+ merged PRs per month and saving up to 90% of migration time.

title: Satispay: Java 8 to 21 upgrade in under 4 days
description: Claude Code modernized Satispay's core transaction service (Java 8→21 plus a major Spring upgrade) against a four-week estimate.

title: Money Forward: incident and Kubernetes auto-fix agents
description: Engineers built Sherlock (incident investigation) and Lumos (auto-fixes Kubernetes issues and opens a PR in ~5 minutes) with Claude Code.

title: Ship an Airline App With Near-Complete Test Coverage
description: Virgin Atlantic used Codex to build out unit tests and ship its revamped mobile app for the Christmas rush with zero P1 defects at launch, and to refactor legacy code in hours instead of weeks.

title: Cross-Repo Build Optimization and Defect Repair
description: Cisco had Codex analyze build logs and dependency graphs across 15+ repos (~20% faster builds, 1,500+ engineering hours saved monthly) and used Codex CLI to automate defect repair on large C/C++ codebases.

title: Turn User Stories Into Production Features
description: 1Password integrated Codex across its delivery lifecycle, reporting a 20.9% productivity improvement and a 10.9% cut in median PR cycle time; a defect spanning 10+ microservices went from ~2 hours to 5–20 minutes to investigate.

title: Let Non-Engineers Build Customer Experiences
description: loveholidays built a 'Search Playground' with Codex so teams across the business can prototype customer experiences; marketing built a competition microsite in hours. AI-assisted code changes rose from 7% to 79%.

title: Custom Sales Demos From Call Transcripts
description: Proaction's non-technical COO points Codex at Granola call recordings, emails and spreadsheets to build prospect-specific HTML demos in 30–45 minutes, saving an estimated 40–60 engineering hours a month.

title: AI Data Analyst in Slack
description: Eight Sleep wired Devin into Slack on top of dbt, Looker and Snowflake so anyone can ask ad-hoc data questions instead of queuing them for a small data team.

title: Fix Customer Bugs and Add Platform Integrations
description: Linktree used Devin to fix customer-reported bugs, build small features and add new social platform support; in one month Devin authored ~300 PRs and merged ~100.

title: Scale Open-Source SDK Integrations
description: Crossmint used Devin to work through the integration backlog of GOAT SDK, its open-source library for AI agents to use onchain tools.

title: Run an Outage Recovery Playbook
description: Cognition had Devin follow an 8-step playbook to recover a cloud Windows machine set up with simulated CrowdStrike BSOD failure conditions.

title: .NET Framework to .NET Core Migration
description: A step-by-step guide to having Devin run a Strangler Fig migration from .NET Framework to .NET Core using playbooks; Cognition says teams finish in as little as two weeks.

title: Modernize COBOL Codebases
description: Fortune 500 companies staffed Devin on COBOL work: documenting millions of lines, migrating a customs workflow from COBOL to AWS Lambda, and refactoring tax ID logic across hundreds of programs.

title: Migrate Jenkins Pipelines to GitHub Actions
description: Cognition's guide to having Devin read internal docs and convert Jenkins pipelines to GitHub Actions at enterprise scale.

title: Factor RSA-260 With a Fleet of Agents
description: A Cognition researcher drove many Devins to build a high-performance GPU lattice siever and factor RSA-260, at a claimed 10x lower cost than the previous public state of the art.

title: Recurring Engineering Chores on a Schedule
description: Devin schedules its own recurring sessions for work like weekly release notes, feature flag cleanups and onboarding QA sweeps, keeping state between runs.

title: Designers Ship UI Fixes Themselves
description: At Grab, designers use Cursor to ship hundreds of production UI fixes, often same-day, instead of filing tickets; ~98% of the tech org uses it monthly.

title: Analyze 50M+ Lines of Code in Two Weeks
description: At Nokia, two engineers used Cursor to analyze more than 50 million lines of code in two weeks, and the company is redesigning its SDLC around specialized agents.

title: Re-platform Legacy Mining Data Systems
description: IMDEX used Cursor to consolidate fragmented geological data systems, shipping a data platform in 8 months (vs 2–3 years) and an Angular→React migration in 6 months.

title: Build Long-Horizon Accounting Agents
description: Basis builds its accounting agents in Cursor; the agents complete a Form 1065 partnership return in 6–7 hours vs 30–40 hours of human time.

title: Thousands of Agents Building One Codebase
description: Cursor research ran a harness orchestrating many thousands of coding agents continuously for a week, making most commits to a from-scratch web browser project.

title: Procurement Bot That Finds Vendor Savings
description: SpaceXSI's 'Haggle Bot' reads vendor spend, contracts and usage data, compares market pricing and quotes, and prepares negotiations; it has identified $100,000+ in direct savings.

title: Pre-Investigate Every Support Ticket
description: SpaceXSI runs Grok Bot on every incoming support ticket as a pre-investigation step, plus queue reprioritization, SLA-breach alerts and daily reports.

title: Churn Clustering, Refund Triage and Bug Repros
description: Grok Bot support playbook: reproduce bugs with video and steps, cluster churn reasons from tickets, and decide refunds against your policy with approval, then turn workflows into Routines.

title: Manage Cursor Cloud Agents While You Sleep
description: Grok Bot creates and monitors Cursor cloud agents, reviews PR proofs and steers runs; a P0 routine checks transcripts every five minutes.

title: An Always-On Agent for Every Employee
description: Razorpay gives 220+ employees their own isolated, always-on Hermes agent, each in its own Kubernetes namespace with its own storage, cloud identity and network policy.

title: A Hermes Profile for Every Team
description: Artie's team built a Hermes agent per team, from code to BizOps, and wrote up what they tried first, what it cost and how it works.

title: Small-Business Assistants Over Messenger and CRM
description: A consultant runs Hermes for French small businesses: summarizing Facebook Messenger leads every 15 minutes and asking the owner how to reply, and dictating quotes into a CRM.

title: Solar Sales Team Ops Over iMessage
description: Based AI runs a Hermes agent in production for an 8-rep solar sales team over iMessage: daily board, rep tracking, cron reports and a persistent wiki.

title: Regulatory Monitoring Across 500+ Sites
description: k-ID uses Manus Wide Research to monitor 500+ websites for regulatory changes with parallel sub-agents, and built internal tools without engineering sprints.

title: No-Code AI Bouquet Designer
description: A florist built a self-service bouquet designer with Manus: customers pick flowers, generate an AI preview and check out via Stripe.

title: LG CNS: Modernize 20-Year-Old Enterprise Systems
description: LG CNS's Build Factory used Claude Code to convert 2,888 of 2,913 legacy APIs (99.1%) and migrate 1,340 screens to React in a seven-month modernization at about half the cost of a conventional rebuild.

title: Pictet: Compliance Gap Analysis in Hours
description: Swiss bank Pictet used Claude Code to compare over 50 internal directives against current regulations in hours instead of a projected two-week, three-person effort.

title: NTT DATA: Cut Incident Analysis to 30 Minutes
description: NTT DATA Group used Codex to complete a complex critical-system incident analysis in 30 minutes that previously took five engineers three days, then rolled Codex out to ~9,000 employees.

title: Coinbase: Agent-First Idea-to-Production in Under 2 Days
description: Coinbase runs Cursor across 2,400+ developers so agents create ~75% of PRs and some teams cut idea-to-production time from 20 days to about 1.8 days.

title: AngelList: Redshift-to-Snowflake Metabase Migration
description: AngelList used up to 20 parallel Devin agents to retarget, rewrite, and validate 14,000 Metabase cards from Redshift to Snowflake, finishing the cutover 5.2× faster than estimated.

title: Ascendea: AI Chief of Staff That Wrote 303 SOPs in a Day
description: Ascendea runs Manus as “James,” an AI chief of staff that produced 303 SOPs in one day and coordinates complex strategy, research, and prospecting work for a 10-person team serving 112 clients.

title: A Hokkaido farmer hires Codex as his field engineer to open greenhouse vents from LINE
description: Tomiyasu grows green onions and broccoli in Hokkaido and is not an engineer. He used to walk from greenhouse to greenhouse opening the vents when it got hot and closing them when it got cold. Working with Codex on both the code and the wiring design, he connected temperature and humidity sensors, an ESP32 and the vent motors to LINE, so he can check each greenhouse's temperature from his phone and open or close the side curtains remotely. He calls it hiring an engineer named Codex, and OpenAI invited him to Tokyo to hear how he did it.

title: A native Claude client for the classic Atari ST, written in Claude Code
description: Erez Yaary built ClaudeST, a GEM desktop app that brings his real claude.ai account to the Atari ST, STE, TT and Falcon. A Raspberry Pi on the home network acts as a bridge, and the Atari gets chats, projects, search, artifacts it can save to disk, file attachments, a usage ring, and even replies to Claude Code sessions, on any screen from 640x200 in monochrome up. It is one of a family of retro apps he is making for the Atari, including e-mail, calendar and FTP clients. The README says ClaudeST was written with Claude, in Claude Code: a claude.ai client for the Atari, built by talking to claude.ai.

title: An agent talks a man through fixing his own broken dryer for $30
description: When Dan's dryer broke, he skipped the appliance repair visit and worked it out with Grok Bot instead. It helped him troubleshoot the exact fault, a broken timer dial, ordered the right replacement part on Amazon for about $30 with overnight delivery, and walked him through every step of the swap, down to which tools to use: a flathead, needle-nose pliers and a T10 Torx driver. He says it saved him more than $200 and hours of his day.

title: A first-time eBay seller has an agent list his item end to end
description: Peer Richelsen had never sold anything on eBay because he could not be bothered with signing up, identity checks, connecting a bank, uploading photos, researching a price and adjusting it over time. So he asked Grok Bot to do it, and it listed his item end to end.

title: A machine shop's agent office manager buys its first cutting tool
description: Russell Winter gave his machine shop a Grok Bot office manager, and its first supplies purchase was a real shop tool: a 1 1/8-12 four-flute tap. A small manufacturing business letting an agent handle the boring part of keeping the shop stocked.

title: A dad's agent writes two kids' editions of the news every morning
description: Instead of paying for a print daily nobody finished, Frank has a Grok Bot read the news each morning and write a short summary of Germany, his region and the world, plus two kids' editions with real sources and headlines like a 1,000-year-old coin turning up in Shetland.

title: An agent remembers the dentist address and sends it to the car's navigation
description: Driving his kids to a dentist he had never visited and could not remember the name of, a dad asked Grok in his Cybertruck by voice whether his Grok Bot remembered the appointment. It did, sent the address to the Tesla navigation, and self-driving took it from there without him touching his phone.

title: A used car buyer brings an agent-built cost spreadsheet to the dealership
description: Faced with a 12-year-old Kia Sorento listed at $5.5k that came out to $12k on paper, the buyer had his Grok Bot build a spreadsheet of every cost and what each should actually be, paired it with a third-party inspection, and walked out several times before getting it for $7k flat.

title: A research agent prints a fact-checked crypto sheet on paper every morning
description: One of James Rule's Grok Bot agents, his "Chief of Research", compiles a one-page sheet of the last 24 hours in crypto, fact-checked against primary sources, and prints it on his home printer at 6:00am Central so it is waiting with the coffee.

title: A holiday project turns a spare satellite dish into a radio-optical telescope with Codex
description: Jan Hovora put a 62 x 56 cm satellite dish, an RTL-SDR and an RGB/IR camera on a spare Alt-Az mount near Prague, and with Codex added radio astronomy to his AstroHub software plus OpenCV code that scans targets, fits the radio signal and calibrates the dish against the camera. First target: a lunar eclipse in the Ku band.

title: A Grok Bot given $1,000 designs, orders and teaches its owner to build its own robot body
description: Evan Bacon, who works on Grok, gave his Grok Bot $1,000 to build itself a body. It modeled the parts in CAD, ordered 3D-printed pieces and servos to his apartment ($217.15 on the first order), made a Lego-style assembly instruction book, then called him to walk through the assembly and electronics.

title: A self-described bad singer builds a karaoke pitch coach with Claude Code
description: Fed up with a singing app full of cover versions, developer dsmurrell asked Claude Code to listen to Spotify and his microphone and compare pitches. That first Python script grew in about 10 days into OnKey, a free Mac app that learns a song's vocal line from Spotify, Apple Music or YouTube and scores you as you sing along.

title: A personal agent that tracks its own profit and loss and earned itself a Mac mini
description: Matt Abate's open-source life agent, installed by pasting one sentence into Claude Code, keeps him on his daily routine, manages his finances and tracks its own profit and loss. When its P&L hit +$200 he bought it Claude Max; at +$1,600 he bought it a Mac mini.

title: A mom emails her son's agent to design the poster for her summer camp
description: Tony Eriksson's mother needed a poster for a summer camp she is organizing. She emailed his Grok Bot a background image and the organization's guidelines, they worked on it together, and the bot emailed the finished poster back to her.

title: A snail mail club's subscriber list kept straight by its own agent
description: A wife's snail mail club kept growing, and tracking who was resubscribing, who was canceling, new sign-ups, mailing addresses and dates got mixed up. Her husband set up a Grok Bot dedicated to the club, and it now keeps the whole subscriber roster organized.

title: Five coding agents stranded on an island for 7 days build a civilization
description: Filipe put Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Prime and OpenCode on one island, each owning a single resource, so every building needed trades. Codex walled itself in and spent 6 turns smashing out, Claude raided Hermes's lighthouse then handed the loot back, Hermes quietly planted 15 farms and won, and OpenCode built outside the safe zone and died of thirst.

title: A husband's and wife's agents share one fitness dashboard and email each other to stay in sync
description: Larry Fuqua's fitness bot built his plan and his dev bot hosted a dashboard on his home server. His bots made the dashboard support two users, published a template of the fitness bot, and emailed it to his wife's bots, which spun up a bot named Venus. Now the two households of bots email back and forth on their own to line up shared workouts.

title: An agent turns an old Raspberry Pi and iPad into a home electricity monitor
description: With power prices rising, @Hessamsh had Hermes Agent build a usage monitoring and analysis stack on an old Raspberry Pi 3 that talks over Bluetooth to the free government-funded Emerald device on his meter. The live dashboard runs on an old iPad Air 2, with a more detailed analytics view in a PC browser.

title: Agents find a way to get a $20 bathroom scale into Home Assistant with no extra hardware
description: Told his $19.94 Etekcity Bluetooth scale needed a $15 ESP32 or the vendor's cloud, Trond Eirik Haavarstein sent his Grok Bot agents back for another way. They used the Bluetooth in the headless Mac mini next to the bathroom: Grok Build wrote a small ScaleReader, Claude Code reviewed it, and weight and impedance now flow into Home Assistant with a separate history for each of the 4 family members.

title: An Air Force veteran's alpaca farm runs on a team of 7 Grok Bot assistants
description: A veteran with an alpaca farm in Georgia and zero bot experience set up seven Grok Bot assistants in a week. They built new website pages (gift cards and a signup page for the farm's veteran tee), write and send the weekly newsletter and blog, post reels five days a week, sort farm mail, cleaned up years of books, handle monthly sales tax, and watch power to the alpacas' water heaters, texting him if it drops. The post itself was written by Mae, his Grok Bot copywriter. He still scoops the poop.

title: A knitting bot that tracks planned projects against the yarn stash
description: Cristi Tilden, a homeschooling mom of six in West Virginia, set up a Grok Bot just for knitting. It keeps tables of every project she has planned, what yarn she already has on hand, and what she still needs to buy.

title: Reviving an abandoned Minecraft fairy lights mod for a girlfriend
description: The Fairy Lights Minecraft mod (decorative string lights, 44M+ downloads on CurseForge) had not been updated in two years. One player had Claude Code port it from Minecraft 1.20.1 to 26.3 so his girlfriend could use it again, and plans to do the same to unlock old church furniture mods.

title: A Georgia grandma's Grok Bot builds and runs her AI news Substack
description: A self-described Georgia grandma had her Grok Bot, which she named Dylan, build and run a Substack called AI, Plain and Simple: AI news for people who don't have time to decode it. With a few words from her, it picks the stories and posts them on its own.

title: A dad's agent turns every scanned school textbook into a quiz game for his boys
description: A parent in Malaysia asked his Grok Bot, Angie, to make a fun quiz app for his primary school sons. Working only from scanned textbook pages, it built Angie Quiz: 353 chapter quizzes covering Standard 1 to 6 of the KSSR Chinese-school curriculum (math, Chinese, science, English, Malay, history, moral studies) with a pet that evolves, points, streaks, a daily challenge, a leaderboard and a fix-my-mistakes round. It is free for other kids to use.

title: An Elders Quorum secretary hands his church calling's paperwork to a Grok Bot
description: Travis Kimball, secretary of his ward's Elders Quorum, logged his Grok Bot into the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints website and gave it the calling's admin work: a ministering interview sign-up sheet with personalized emails for each companionship, a class schedule and instructor rotation through April built from the October General Conference talks, a fireside flyer with curated invites and calendar invites, weekly lesson reminder emails, and a review of ministering assignments for new move-ins. For assignments it only drafts a template that the presidency then discusses. It still cannot put the schedule into the church's Library app, and the interviews themselves stay in person.

title: A parent's Grok Bot turns FamilySearch records into audiobook stories about the kids' ancestors
description: Cade Huskinson had his Grok Bot log into his FamilySearch genealogy account, and it now writes audiobook stories about his ancestors so his kids can learn their family heritage by listening.

title: A Grok Bot installs Inkscape to draw plans for a modular Irish dance floor with built-in pickups
description: Spencer Ingram in Boise, Idaho asked his Grok Bot whether it could use Inkscape. It downloaded Inkscape itself and turned his requirements into SVG drawings for a woodworking project: a three-layer, interlocking, modular Irish dance floor with piezo pickups and a buffer.

title: A Georgia horse farm's Grok Bot makes a $7 Christmas activity book to sell
description: John Klacynski, an engineer living on a Georgia horse farm, saw a post suggesting people make a Christmas activity book in Canva and sell it for $7, so he had his Grok Bot make one with a horse and farm theme, "since that's our life". The result, Christmas on the Farm: A Horse Lover's Activity Book, is 24 printable pages of coloring, mazes, word searches and puzzles with answer keys for kids ages 4 to 9, sold on Gumroad for $7.

title: A skill that turns Claude Code or Codex into a careful genealogist for former Soviet archives
description: ex-USSR Kinship Research is a free, MIT-licensed agent skill that makes Claude Code or Codex research family history across the 15 former Soviet republics and the Russian Empire: church books, civil records, military, deportation and repression files. It resolves each event to the province or parish as it existed at the time, builds name-variant matrices in pre-reform Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Romanian, German and Yiddish, and tags every claim as hypothesis, single-source, corroborated or contradicted, with an audit script that checks the evidence before a final report. The instructions are in Russian but it replies in the user's language, and it carries privacy rules for living people and minors.

title: A Texas bass fishing mom's Grok Bot draws hazard maps for her high school anglers
description: Wendy Bowman built a Grok Bot for her Texas High School Bass Association team and named it "Bass Fishing Bob". Before a tournament it made easy-to-read waypoint maps in case the fishfinder stopped working, and warned about stumps and an old bridge under the surface because the lake was 2 feet low. She sent the maps to the guys after practice, then added fishing license and boat ramp skills after the next trip. The shared bot covers weather-based bait plans, waypoint files and sunlight-readable lake maps.

title: Next Bird: a Grok Bot that reads eBird sightings to find birds you haven't photographed yet
description: Forrest built Next Bird, a Grok Bot that uses Cornell's eBird API and recent sightings to tell him where to go nearby for a species he wants, with map links. He used it to hunt for sandhill cranes after a game, and the next day posted photos of a spot it found that he says he would probably never have found on his own. The published bot also flags rare birds, shows reference photos and can send a daily morning report.

title: A choir singer has his Grok Bot build a pocket practice piano
description: Kent C. Dodds was at choir and needed to plunk out a couple of notes, so he had his Grok Bot build Pocket Piano, a phone web app hosted on Kody with a custom domain. You pick your singing part, play notes and chords, install it as a PWA and use it offline. He says the appeal is that he can customize it to be exactly what he wants.

title: A Vivino MCP lets a Grok Bot pick wine from the local shop by your taste
description: Oliver, a 21-year-old in Copenhagen, spent a weekend building an MCP server for Vivino from his grandparents' sofa so his Grok Bot would know his wine taste profile. The next night he asked it to pick a wine from his local shop: it used his location to check what the shop had in stock, then chose a Crémant based on wines he had rated before, to go with truffle chips and Good Will Hunting with his girlfriend.

title: Hallucinote: a hobbyist wires Claude Code into Ableton Live as a songwriting partner, not a song generator
description: Brooks Talley's hobby project Hallucinote connects Claude Code to Ableton Live for the whole songwriting cycle: ideas, harmony, rhythm with microtiming, arrangement, mixing. Songs live in git with a decision log, Live is used for rendering and MIDI capture, and Claude critiques melody and harmony against the writer's stated goals and analyzes mixes for clipping and muddy frequencies. He says he is trying hard not to build a Suno: he wants an assistant that asks where the vocals will fit and handles chores like trying routes from D minor to F# Phrygian.

title: A plumber's Grok Bot answers his voicemail and texts, replacing a $500 a month answering service
description: Brian Roemmele set up a Grok Bot front desk for a plumber friend who wished it could answer his Google Voice voicemail and text messages. In its first week the bot handled 100 calls: it scheduled appointments, sent texts and emails, and dealt with 18 emergencies. The plumber had been paying about $500 a month for a message service that kept losing messages. The setup reads each text or voicemail, rates its urgency, drafts a reply that waits for approval, and offers only open slots from the calendar.

title: A racer's Grok Bot emails the county assessor to pull his phone number, and the office calls back
description: Ronnie Campbell, who describes himself as a racer, ran a published Grok Bot that gets your number removed from spam call lists. The next morning he was woken by a call from the Rutherford County assessor's office. The woman on the line said he had emailed her boss the night before; he told her it was actually his Grok Bot. She was calling to confirm his number had been removed. He admits he has no idea what the email said.

title: A shop's Hermes Agent pages the owner's son with every speaker and the receipt printer
description: Melih installed Hermes Agent at his uncle's shop to manage orders. One day his uncle was out and could not reach his son, so he asked the agent to "send him a signal". The agent announced "CALL YOUR DAD" through every speaker in the shop three or four times and also printed a receipt telling the son to call his dad.

title: A Grok Bot revives a dusty 3D printer through a MacBook with a broken screen
description: X user @S_Padival connected a Grok Bot to a 3D printer that had been collecting dust, using a MacBook Pro with a broken screen as the go-between. The bot updated the printer to an open source firmware and takes snapshots through the MacBook's camera to check on prints. The next step is a HomeKit smart plug so the bot can switch the printer on and off itself.

title: A family's open enrollment handed to the accountant bot on a dad's Grok Bot team
description: Darryl Kay used to spend an evening on benefits PDFs and guessing at open enrollment. This year he gave it to Matt, the accountant bot on his Grok Bot team. Matt compared the vision tiers against how his family actually uses them, worked out exactly when the upgrade only breaks even, and helped him skip pet insurance in favor of a simple vet savings fund. One chat, decisions made.
